# Dynamic Factor Model (DFM) for GDP Nowcasting in South Korea

This repository implements a **Dynamic Factor Model (DFM)** using the **Kalman Filter** and **Maximum Likelihood Estimation** in R to nowcast and forecast quarterly South Korean GDP growth.

## Key Features & Methodology
- **State-Space Modeling:** Combines 10 high-frequency monthly indicators (hard data, survey sentiment, credit spreads) and quarterly GDP into a unified state-space framework.
- **Custom Kalman Filter:** Handles mixed-frequency data, jagged edges, and missing observations (including COVID-19 shock treatment).
- **Automated Model Selection:** Includes a backward stepwise selection algorithm using Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) to identify the optimal parsimonious indicator panel.
- **In-Sample Performance & Forecasting:** Achieves an $R^2 = 0.731$ with a correlation of 0.858 against actual quarterly GDP growth and computes $T+1$ and $T+2$ forecasts with variance confidence intervals.

## File Structure
- `main.R`: Main execution script for data preparation, model fitting, and forecasting.
- `kalman.R`: Custom Kalman filter loop and Gaussian log-likelihood evaluation.
- `estimation.R`: Maximum likelihood parameter optimization using L-BFGS-B.
- `matrices.R`: State-space matrix construction ($H, F, R, Q$) matching variable frequencies.
- `stepwise.R`: Automated BIC-based model optimization.
